gloss: New Year's Eve; the last night of the year

definitions.gloss: New Year's Eve; the last night of the year
definitions.explanation: The night of December 31st. Most commonly encountered in the compound {除夜|じょや}の{鐘|かね} (the New Year's Eve temple bells).

examples.english: The New Year's Eve bells ring.
The New Year's Eve bells are struck 108 times.

examples.japanese: ⟦{毎年|まいとし}→毎年：00731_maitoshi⟧{除夜|じょや}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{鐘|かね}→鐘：02654_kane⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{聞|き}き→聞く：00483_kiku⟧⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧⟦{新年|しんねん}→新年：09787_shinnen⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{迎|むか}える→迎える：01193_mukaeru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{我|わ}が{家|や}→我が家：03038_wagaya⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{習慣|しゅうかん}→習慣：01429_shuukan⟧だ。
examples.english: It's our family's custom to welcome the new year while listening to the New Year's Eve bells.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
{除夜|じょや}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{鐘|かね}→鐘：02654_kane⟧ is one of the most iconic sounds of the Japanese New Year. Buddhist temples ring their bells 108 times — once for each of the 108 worldly desires (⟦{煩悩|ぼんのう}→煩悩：14880_bonnou⟧) in Buddhist teaching. The ringing begins on the night of December 31st and often continues past midnight into the new year. It is broadcast on TV as part of NHK's ⟦{紅白|こうはく}{歌合戦|うたがっせん}→紅白歌合戦：29111_kouhakuutagassen⟧ end-of-year programming.

ETYMOLOGY:
{除|じょ} means "to remove" and {夜|や} means "night." The name refers to the night that removes the old year.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {除夜|じょや}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{鐘|かね}→鐘：02654_kane⟧ (New Year's Eve bells — the most common use by far)
- {除夜|じょや}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{鐘|かね}→鐘：02654_kane⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{撞|つ}く (to ring the New Year's Eve bells)
- {除夜|じょや}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{鐘|かね}→鐘：02654_kane⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{聞|き}く→聞く：00483_kiku⟧ (to listen to the New Year's Eve bells)
